# Marketing campaigns

Which tagged links (`?ref=<name>`) brought visitors, and how many of them searched. Refresh with `npm run umami:campaigns`; the `/campaign-report` skill refreshes it and rewrites the findings.

- **Visits / Visitors**: visits (30 min of inactivity ends one) and distinct browsers. The `ref` counts on the entry page only; a returning visitor without a `ref` is untagged.
- **Searched**: share of visits with at least one search, and how many that is. Measured over visits from 03.07. on, when event tracking started (earlier visits only count towards Visits, e.g. the first Reddit day).
- **Returned**: the same browser came back in a later visit (within Umami's monthly session id).
- † fewer than 20 visits: a rate from so few says nothing.

## Findings

State of 16.11.2026. Rewritten by hand after each refresh (the `/campaign-report` skill does this); the numbers above are generated.

**Answer in one line:** The loky.news newsletter is the strongest single launch so far (234 tagged visits, 173 on the first day, 97 searching visits, the most of any campaign), and it is worth repeating. Quality is the same everywhere: 40–48 % of visits searched on every channel, untagged traffic included (43 %), so the channels differ in volume and timing, not in what the visitors do. The offline tag (sticker) has brought almost nothing.

Changed since 13.11.: loky.news is now a finished burst (173 visits on 13.11., 36 on 14.11., 18 on 15.11., 5 on 16.11.) instead of a first-hours reading; its search rate is 41 %, in line with the rest, and 11 % returned. Untagged traffic also rose on the same days (73, 55, 28 against about 20 a day the week before), probably loky readers who arrived without the `ref` (forwarded mail, typed address, search), but that cannot be proven from the data. The earlier claim that Nebenan.de has the best search rate is dropped: the blog is at 48 %, Nebenan at 45 %, and a difference of a few points is noise.

| Campaign | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|
| loky.news | strongest launch, one-day burst | Newsletter to a local readership went out 13.11. around 06:00. 234 visits (222 visitors), 173 on the day, then a fast tail. 41 % searched (97), the most searching visits of any campaign. 75 % mobile. The link was `?ref=loky.news` (alias to `loky`). Roughly 90 extra untagged visits on 13.–15.11. are probably more of the same audience, so the real reach is likely above 234 |
| Reddit | most visits over time, in bursts | 316 visits since 01.07. Two posts, 01.07. (56 visits that day) and 01.11. (47, 24, 19 over the three days after), each fading within 3 days; the roughly 10 visits a week in mid-September and the 1–7 a day since 09.11. came without a post. Both posts carry the same `ref`, so the report cannot tell them apart beyond the dates. 85 % mobile. 40 % searched (92) |
| Nebenan.de | most dependable | 196 visits over four months, 45 % searched (89). The week of 20.07. alone gave 71 visits (34 on 22.07.). Fewest returners among the big campaigns (12 %) |
| Weddingweiser blog | strong launch, small tail | 141 visits, 65 on 27.10., then 23 and 13, 1–3 a day since. 48 % searched (67), the highest rate of the four, within noise of the others. The 26.–28.10. spike also had the Nebenan discussion and untagged ZLB forum traffic, so it cannot be split cleanly |
| Sticker | not working yet | 14 visits over 3.5 months, 2 of them searched. Too few to judge the idea, enough to say that this placement does not move traffic |
| Slack | one-off test | 15 visits, no conclusion |

Limits of the data: a visit is credited to the `ref` on its entry page only (a returning visitor without a `ref` counts as untagged), so a newsletter that is forwarded or read days later loses attribution; bots cannot be told from bounces, so search rates may be slightly low; events exist since 03.07.; "Returned" for loky.news is only three days old; the labels and channels in `campaigns.json` for `sticker` and `slack` are guesses, please correct them.
